title: Fleet: label + discover burst pools; prevent reservation allocator from consuming burst capacity
author: Vanessa Ortiz
description:
Summary: This PR introduces explicit labeling for burst pools, updates fleet discovery to expose burst pool metadata to downstream consumers, and adds hard safety checks to ensure burst capacity cannot be accidentally allocated as baseline Dedicated reservation capacity. This is the Fleet-side prerequisite for burst-aware routing/admission work (ENG-4825), and it closes a class of failure modes we identified during topology review where a misconfigured pool could silently become eligible for reservation placement.

Context / Motivation: Redwood Dedicated is adding a “burst capacity” option where a Dedicated tenant can temporarily draw from controlled shared burst pools. These pools must remain isolated from baseline Dedicated guarantees and from any reservation allocator logic. Prior to this PR, pool classification was partially implicit (naming conventions + per-cluster config), which is too brittle for a feature that will be operated under incident conditions.

Changes (high level): 1) Pool labeling: Add canonical pool labels emitted by the fleet registry and enforced in provisioner templates. New labels (names are stable and intended for multi-service consumption): - redwood.ai/pool.class = {dedicated_baseline|dedicated_burst|hosted|internal} - redwood.ai/pool.region = <region> - redwood.ai/pool.gpu_type = <gpu sku> - redwood.ai/pool.isolation = {tenant|shared} - redwood.ai/pool.burst_eligible = {true|false} (derived; true iff pool.class == dedicated_burst)

2) Pool discovery API: Extend FleetDiscovery response to include pool.class, burst_eligible, and isolation. Add query filters to support downstream usage patterns: - includeBurstPools (default false for safety; must be explicitly opted-in) - requireIsolation=tenant|shared (used by allocators/schedulers) Note: Existing callers that list pools for reservation placement continue to see only baseline Dedicated pools (and hosted/internal as before) unless includeBurstPools=true.

3) Reservation allocator guardrails: Add a deny-by-default check in reservation placement: if a pool is labeled dedicated_burst OR isolation==shared, it is rejected as a placement target regardless of other predicates. This is intentionally redundant with the discovery default (belt + suspenders). Add a startup-time sanity validation that fails fast (and pages) if the allocator is configured with includeBurstPools=true in production.

4) Sanity checks + observability: - New periodic “pool invariants” checker that verifies: (a) any pool.class==dedicated_burst has isolation==shared, (b) burst pools are not in the “reserved capacity eligible” set, (c) there is no overlap between baseline pool IDs and burst pool IDs within a region/gpu_type tuple. - Emit counters for invariant violations and placement rejections with a stable reason code: fleet_allocator_reject_total{reason="burst_pool"|"shared_isolation"|"missing_labels"|...}. - Add log fields to placement decision logs: pool_class, burst_eligible, isolation.

Implementation notes: - Label definitions live in pkg/fleet/labels with a single source of truth (consts + validation helpers). - Provisioner templates updated to set labels at pool creation time; we also support backfill via a one-off migration command for existing pools (see scripts/fleet/backfill_pool_labels.go). - Discovery API version bump is backwards compatible (new fields are optional; defaults apply).

Testing: - Unit tests: label validation, discovery filtering behavior, allocator rejection predicates, invariant checker. - Integration: a small fake registry + allocator test that asserts a burst pool cannot be used to satisfy a reservation request even when capacity is available. - Added regression test to ensure includeBurstPools defaults to false.

Rollout / Ops: - This PR is safe to roll out ahead of routing/policy changes. Existing Dedicated baseline behavior is unchanged. - After deploy, Fleet team will run the label backfill job in 3 pilot regions and validate invariants dashboards. - Follow-ups: ENG-4828 (cooldowns/circuit breaker) will rely on pool.class and burst_eligible fields; routing will consume discovery includeBurstPools=true only in the burst admission path.

Files / Areas changed (representative): - pkg/fleet/labels/* - pkg/fleet/discovery/service.go - pkg/fleet/discovery/types.go - pkg/dedicated/allocator/placement.go - pkg/dedicated/allocator/sanity_checks.go - scripts/fleet/backfill_pool_labels.go - pkg/fleet/invariants/checker.go

Commits: 1) fleet: introduce pool label schema + validation helpers 2) provisioner: stamp pool.class + isolation labels at creation 3) discovery: expose pool.class/burst_eligible; add includeBurstPools filter 4) allocator: hard reject burst/shared pools; add fail-fast config guard 5) invariants: periodic checker + metrics + logs 6) tests: discovery/allocator coverage

Review notes: - We intentionally made includeBurstPools opt-in and added allocator-level hard rejects to prevent a “single config knob” from mixing baseline and burst pools. - Naming: used pool.class instead of pool.type to avoid collision with existing internal “node type” usage.

Linked work: - ENG-4825 (this PR) - ENG-4821 (initiative umbrella)

Release note (internal): Fleet now labels burst pools explicitly and prevents Dedicated reservation allocator from placing capacity into burst pools; adds invariant checks + metrics for pool classification drift.
conversation:
Keiko Yamamoto (review): Can we make the allocator reject based on isolation==shared even if pool.class is missing? That seems safer during backfill windows. Vanessa Ortiz (author): Yep — added a predicate that rejects shared isolation unconditionally, and missing labels fall back to conservative reject with reason="missing_labels" for placement paths.

Nina Petrova (review): Are we confident the label names are stable and won’t conflict with k8s reserved label keys? Please avoid “pool-type” style labels without a domain prefix. Vanessa Ortiz (author): Good call. Updated all labels to use redwood.ai/* domain and added a small validator to block non-prefixed variants.

Mina Haddad (review): Discovery defaulting to includeBurstPools=false is good. Can you confirm routing will still be able to request burst pools without needing a separate endpoint? Vanessa Ortiz (author): Yes — same endpoint, new includeBurstPools flag. Routing will opt-in only on the burst admission path.

Sean Gallagher (review): For the startup-time sanity validation, please make sure it’s a loud signal but not a crash loop if someone toggles the flag accidentally in a canary. Prefer: refuse to start in prod, warn in staging/dev. Vanessa Ortiz (author): Implemented environment-gated behavior: prod => fatal with explicit log + metric; non-prod => warning + metric.

Samantha Roy (review): Metric cardinality: reason codes are fine, but please don’t add pool_id as a label. Vanessa Ortiz (author): Agreed — counters use stable reason only; pool_id stays in logs/traces.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Any security implications if labels are missing/incorrect? I want the safe default to be deny. Vanessa Ortiz (author): Placement is deny-by-default when pool.class is absent; discovery also excludes burst pools unless explicitly requested.

Keiko Yamamoto (approve): Looks good after the shared-isolation guard + env gating. Approved.

Sean Gallagher (approve): Approved — thanks for making the prod behavior fail fast.

Vanessa Ortiz (merge): Squash merged to main.
